title: International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy Nutrition
excerpt: Oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens, and citrus — practical ways to build balanced plates.
content:
## Introduction to Pregnancy Nutrition
Pregnancy nutrition plays a crucial role in ensuring the health of both mother and baby. A balanced and varied diet will provide the necessary nutrients for fetal development. In this article, we will explore international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy, helping to build balanced and safe meals.

## International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy
The following international pantry staples are excellent choices for pregnant women:
- Oats: rich in fiber, supporting digestive health and reducing the risk of constipation.
- Greek yogurt: rich in calcium, supporting the development of bones and teeth in the fetus.
- Lentils: rich in iron, supporting the production of red blood cells and reducing the risk of anemia.
- Low-mercury salmon: rich in omega-3 fatty acids, supporting the development of the brain and eyes in the fetus.
- Eggs: rich in protein, supporting the development of muscles and tissues in the fetus.
- Leafy greens and citrus: rich in vitamins and minerals, supporting the immune system and reducing the risk of disease.

## Combining International Pantry Staples into Meals
To combine these international pantry staples into meals, you can try the following:
- Add oats to breakfast with Greek yogurt and fruit.
- Use lentils to make stews or soups.
- Cook low-mercury salmon with leafy greens and citrus to create a balanced meal.
- Add eggs to meals with leafy greens and citrus to create a protein-rich meal.

## Food Safety during Pregnancy
When pregnant, ensuring food safety is crucial. You should avoid the following foods:
- Raw or undercooked foods, such as sushi or raw meat.
- Foods high in mercury, such as shark or swordfish.
- Foods containing listeria, such as soft cheese or cold cuts.

## Conclusion
Pregnancy nutrition is a vital part of prenatal care. By incorporating international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy into meals, you can help ensure the health of both mother and baby. Always prioritize food safety and consult with your doctor or a registered dietitian to develop a balanced and safe diet.
